one_line: A WebMCP-powered workspace that turns scattered launch feedback into evidence-linked product decisions and follow-up actions.
what_it_does: Signal Desk presents a triage workflow for importing customer feedback, grouping recurring pain, drafting a customer-impact brief, proposing product-owned actions, and maintaining a decision log/audit trail.
leverage_rationale: The structured triage and evidence-linked action workflow appears to make agent operations more repeatable and reviewable than generic UI driving, but the packet does not demonstrate the live tools or shared state end to end.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes an 8-tool WebMCP surface and an evidence-backed triage workflow.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows a search_signals modelContext.executeTool call and workflow stages for finding patterns and deciding follow-up.
Approval/review and decision-log behavior are claimed but not independently demonstrated in the still evidence.
execution_rationale: The packaging is coherent and the screenshot shows a purpose-built workflow with concrete stages, but there is no submitted video and the screenshot is a Devpost page/video thumbnail, so central execution and edge-state completeness remain unverified.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a coherent Signal Desk interface concept with customer requests, pain patterns, impact brief, product actions, and decision log.
The visible instruction describes running triage to group requests, draft the brief, propose actions, and update the decision log.
No video frame sheets or transcript were submitted; the product is not directly exercised in the available evidence.
impact_rationale: Support, product, and launch teams have a specific recurring problem—turning distributed feedback into defensible decisions—and the proposed evidence-linked workflow addresses that problem directly.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets messy launch feedback and evidence-backed product actions.
Description identifies support tickets, community posts, sales calls, and release comments as inputs.
Visible workflow connects repeated customer pain to an impact brief, follow-up action, and decision log.
creativity_rationale: The notable angle is combining customer-feedback synthesis with evidence provenance, approval-gated action review, and governance/auditability rather than presenting generic summarization.
creativity_evidence: Submission frames the product around preventing agents from quietly doing the wrong thing after operating an app.
The visible concept integrates evidence-linked claims, product-owned follow-up, and a decision log.
The submission explicitly presents governance as a core stress test for agent workflows.
usability_note: The staged workflow appears understandable and review-oriented, but usability of the live product cannot be verified from the packaging screenshot alone.
red_flags: No video evidence was submitted despite a video thumbnail being visible on the Devpost screenshot.
Many claims about approval gates, audit trail, fallback, deployment, and testing are not directly verifiable in the packet.
standouts: Strong evidence/provenance and governance framing for agent-assisted product triage.
Clear mapping from recurring feedback to reviewable product action.
advance_reason: A credible, high-value workflow with a meaningful structured-agent delta and a distinctive governance angle; advance while treating execution as claimed rather than observed.

one_line: A browser-based voxel data-center builder and simulator that exposes infrastructure-building operations to AI agents through WebMCP.
what_it_does: The project describes designing a 32×8×32 voxel data center, simulating facility behavior and resource projections, checking standards, generating a schema manifest, and publishing a certification verdict while withholding the design.
leverage_rationale: For structured infrastructure construction, standards checks, manifest generation, and simulation, WebMCP can give an agent precise domain operations and state access that would be materially less reliable through generic browser control. The packet does not fully prove the privacy/zero-knowledge boundary or complete agent loop.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says WebMCP lets AI agents manipulate infrastructure on the frontend monitor.
About text describes six tool-oriented steps including building the data center, checking regulations, generating a schema manifest, simulation, and a ChatGPT desktop agent flow.
Video frames visibly show a browser 3D environment with persistent grid/arena state, changing viewpoint/object state, and diagnostic or code/log panels.
execution_rationale: The video visibly supports a functioning browser 3D scene with changing state and inspection panels, and the written scope is ambitious and coherent. However, the demo link is dead, frame text is unreadable, and the packet does not establish the full build→simulate→standards→certification flow.
execution_evidence: Three contact sheets show a consistent browser-based 3D editor/simulation across sequential frames.
Frames show camera changes, a persistent gridded environment, an in-world object, and auxiliary text/debug panels.
Submission claims a 32×8×32 grid, 47 block types, deterministic simulation, and 37 standards-backed rules, but these details are not all visible in the frames.
FACTS report the demo link as dead.
impact_rationale: Data-center designers, operators, and auditors have a concrete need to evaluate facility layouts and compliance while protecting commercially sensitive designs. A deterministic simulation and verdict-only certification concept could provide substantial value if the claimed privacy guarantees hold.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies the tension between confidential facility layouts and certification/audit disclosure requirements.
About text names concrete operational outputs: power, thermal, staffing, OPEX, carbon, water, and standards compliance.
The stated workflow targets infrastructure design and compliance rather than a speculative general audience.
creativity_rationale: This is an unusually ambitious synthesis of voxel/SimCity-like data-center design, standards-based deterministic scoring, privacy-preserving certification, and agent operation through WebMCP. The concept is memorable even though the evidence of depth is incomplete.
creativity_evidence: The project combines a 3D voxel facility builder with international data-center standards and simulation.
The submission connects agent transcript/privacy concerns with zero-knowledge-style verdict publication.
The written scope spans construction, simulation, regulatory checks, manifest generation, and certification.
usability_note: The visual editor and panels suggest an inspectable interactive tool, but the small frames and dead live demo prevent judging onboarding, controls, and end-to-end usability.
red_flags: Video frames show a 3D editor/simulation but do not clearly show WebMCP invocations, standards results, certification, or privacy-preserving output.
Small text in the panels is unreadable, limiting verification of the claimed workflow.
standouts: Distinctive data-center-as-voxel-builder concept with real standards and operational simulation.
Ambitious attempt to make agent access and design confidentiality part of the same product problem.
advance_reason: The concept and apparent 3D implementation are unusually ambitious, with a strong potential WebMCP role; advance for deeper observation while discounting unverified end-to-end and privacy claims.
